_source: captured from `git show origin/main:cloudbuild.yaml` at 0910192 (FC-081 merged). This fixture pins MAIN's deploy flags. FC-084 intentionally adds --revision-suffix on top of them; that exception is declared in ALLOWED_NEW_DEPLOY_FLAGS in tests/test_cloudbuild_contract.py. Regenerate only alongside a deliberate, reviewed deploy-flag change.
_deviations: One value here is deliberately NOT main's: `timeout` is 1500s, main is 1200s. FC-084 raises it because a build that waits for an older one needs ~1158s worst case (wait <=798s for the older build + its own ~360s deploy chain), which left only ~42s of headroom under 1200s. Both adversarial reviews called the original 1200s must-not-change a plan defect. serialize-builds' BUILD_TIMEOUT_SECONDS is asserted equal to this value by test_gate_deadline_tracks_the_build_timeout. SECOND DEVIATION (FC-060 Layer 3): `deploy-sweep-job` is added to `step_ids` (LAST, behind all three promotes) and `wait_for`, and `deploy-dashboard-canary`'s `--set-env-vars` gains `SWEEP_JOB_NAME=backtest-sweep`. The env VALUE is part of the frozen flag string, so it cannot be absorbed by ALLOWED_NEW_DEPLOY_FLAGS the way a new flag NAME can - a deliberate env change to a service has to be re-frozen here, in the reviewed commit that makes it. `--set-env-vars` replaces the whole env set, so the value is edited in place rather than appended: dropping any of the four existing entries would silently unset them on the dashboard. Its position is load-bearing: the step can fail because the build service account lacks run.jobs.create, and placed anywhere earlier that failure would abort the build before the wheel/CC/dashboard revisions got their traffic — an ad-hoc measurement tool taking production deploys down with it. Behind the promotes it still fails the build loudly, but only after the services are out. THIRD DEVIATION (FC-096 Phase A): `deploy-backfill-job` is added to `step_ids` and `wait_for`, behind the same three promotes as `deploy-sweep-job` and for the same reason (a `run.jobs.create` failure must not strand a service deploy). The build now has TWO tail steps, so `test_sweep_job_runs_after_every_service_promote`'s `ids[-1] == 'deploy-sweep-job'` assertion was redesigned into `test_the_job_steps_are_the_tail_and_nothing_hides_behind_them`, which pins the tail as the SET `{deploy-sweep-job, deploy-backfill-job}` and re-checks each one's promote edges and marker-first script. Their order relative to each other is deliberately not asserted: they waitFor the same steps and Cloud Build runs them concurrently. NO pre-existing `waitFor` edge changed, and no deploy flag on any service changed. FOURTH DEVIATION (FC-096 Phase A): `deploy-bot-canary`'s `--set-env-vars` gains `CHAIN_LAKE_BUCKET=options-wheel-chain-lake`. This is an ENV-STRING change to a pre-existing step, so — exactly like the SWEEP_JOB_NAME change above — it cannot be absorbed by ALLOWED_NEW_DEPLOY_FLAGS (that mechanism forgives a new flag NAME, never a changed VALUE) and is re-frozen here in the reviewed commit that makes it. Why the wheel service needs it: /regression's `lake_freshness` check reads CHAIN_LAKE_BUCKET, and without it the check warns `lake_freshness_unconfigured` for ever - a detective control that looks alive and watches nothing. It must be in this literal list because --set-env-vars replaces the whole env set, so an out-of-band `services update` survives only until the next merge. The value is edited in place, appended to the existing three entries; dropping any of them would silently unset them on the wheel service. Deliberately NOT added to `deploy-cc-canary`: the covered-call profile has no stocks.symbols, so its copy of the check degrades to a `lake_freshness_no_universe` warn by design - the lake is the wheel's data and the wheel's check is its watcher.
